gui.intel_corrupted_msg:
Detected that your CPU is affected by a critical Intel chip bug.

If you are not familiar with this issue, it is highly recommended to read this $LINK.INTEL_CHIP_BUG_FAQ$. DO NOT report this crash until you have:
  • Updated your BIOS.
  • Made sure that the crash is not caused by this bug, as the issue won't be resolved even after a BIOS update if the CPU has already started dying. It is important to note that this update will not fix damaged hardware. If the PC has crashed or been unstable due to this issue, the CPU is damaged.
  • If the CPU is damaged, replace it under warranty. Intel has extended the warranty for affected processors by two years.
This warning doesn't indicate that this crash is 100% caused by this issue, but before reporting, you must check that a corrupted CPU is not the reason.
gui.duplicated_mod_warn:
If you are seeing this message while trying to run the modpack,it means the modpack
installation is corrupted (possibly due to an incorrect update). To fix this, you need to reinstall the modpack.

Detected multiple mods with mod_id "crash_assistant", leave only one of them:
warnings.atio6axx: The atio6axx "Problematic frame" in a $LOG_FILENAME$ file, is part of the AMD driver for the GPU, there's a bad version of the AMD drivers that instantly crashes on an OpenGL task. Reinstall/Fresh install your drivers from $LINK.AMD_SUPPORT$ IF you do not have an AMD GPU, then you need to set your system to be using that GPU instead of the AMD integrated GPU on the CPU, steps below. $LINK.HOW_FORCE_APP_USE_DISCRETE_GPU$
warnings.jemalloc: The jemalloc "Problematic frame" in $LOG_FILENAME$ indicates an issue with the jemalloc memory allocator. To resolve this, add the following argument to your launcher: -Dorg.lwjgl.system.allocator=system
warnings.libglfw_so: The libglfw.so "Problematic frame" in a $LOG_FILENAME$ file is a typical Linux problem. To fix it, follow the steps below: 1. Download the latest GLFW library files from your distro's official repositories. If you are on a slow updating distro (like Ubuntu), instead download the latest pre-built files from this $LINK.GLFW_DOWNLOAD$ 2. Add -Dorg.lwjgl.glfw.libname=/path/to/file to your launcher java arguments. An example of what this might look like is -Dorg.lwjgl.glfw.libname=/home/frontear/Downloads/libglfw.so. $LANG.warnings_common.so_vm_options$
warnings.libopenal_so: The libopenal.so "Problematic frame" in a $LOG_FILENAME$ file is a typical Linux problem. To fix it, follow the steps below: 1. Download the latest OpenAL library files from your distro's official repositories. 2. Add -Dorg.lwjgl.openal.libname=/usr/lib/libopenal.so to your launcher java arguments. This path might differ depending on your distribution, so please double-check. $LANG.warnings_common.so_vm_options$
warnings.macjdk: The v ~StubRoutines::SafeFetch32 "Problematic Frame" error in $LOG_FILENAME$ is caused by an issue with the bundled Java runtime ("Microsoft" build version 17.0.8 and newer) on Apple Silicon (M1/M2/etc.) CPUs, which causes Java to crash under certain conditions. To resolve this issue, you first need to install a different Java runtime: 1. Click $LINK.AZUL_DOWNLOAD$ to get the recommended Java version for your system. 2. Hover the Download button and click ".dmg" to download the installer. 3. Open the downloaded file and follow the installation instructions. Next, you need to configure your Minecraft launcher to use the newly installed Java. The following instructions are for $LINK.ATL$ and may vary for other launchers: 1. Click "Settings" on the right. 2. Select "Java/Minecraft" at the top. 3. Uncheck "Use Java Provided by Minecraft". 4. Manually enter the following Java path in the "Java Install Location" text box: /Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/zulu-21.jdk/Contents/Home/bin/java
warnings.insufficient_memory: The There is insufficient memory... message in the $LOG_FILENAME$ file means: Your system is running out of available physical RAM or swap space. To fix this, make sure your memory isn't heavily used by other running applications — check using Task Manager, and try to keep unnecessary programs closed while playing Minecraft. Ensure you are using the recommended memory settings for this modpack — perhaps your Xmx value is set too high? If you followed some dumb internet advices about disabling page files, revert it — that's likely the cause. Sometimes, simply restarting your computer can help clear out memory and reset swap usage. If you're using more than the recommended memory settings for this pack, try lowering them. If none of this helps
warnings.insufficient_memory_indv: try the following: * Installing the FerriteCore mod * Installing the ModernFix mod with dynamic_resources and deduplicate_location enabled. * Removing some mods to reduce Minecraft's RAM usage
warnings.out_of_memory_error: The java.lang.OutOfMemoryError message in the $LOG_FILENAME$ file means: There isn't enough memory allocated for Minecraft to continue running. Look up the recommended memory settings for this modpack and allocate more memory. If you're sure you've allocated enough RAM
warnings.closed_by_windows: If this crash happened during game or level loading, it was likely caused by pressing keys or clicking the mouse. The error "The program javaw.exe version ... stopped interacting with Windows and was closed" in $LOG_FILENAME$ means the game froze, possibly due to these actions. To avoid this, let the game load fully—DO NOT CLICK ANYTHING, PRESS ANY KEY, or CLICK END PROCESS. If the crash occurred during mid-gameplay, just press OK and ignore this message.
warnings.curseforge_corrupted: We detected signs in the $LOG_FILENAME$ that your Minecraft installation is corrupted by CurseForge. To fix it, follow the steps below: 1. Open your modpack folder in File Explorer. 2. Go up two levels. 3. Nuke the Install folder. Another solution is switching to another launcher that doesn't have such problems, like $LINK.ATL$.
warnings.resource_location_exception: We detected signs in the $LOG_FILENAME$ that your game encountered a resource location error: Caused by: net.minecraft.ResourceLocationException: Non [a-z0-9/._-] character in path of location. This typically happens when Minecraft tries to load a resource (such as a block, item, or texture) using a name that includes invalid characters, often caused by non-English system language settings. To fix this, add the following JVM arguments to force the game to use English locale settings: -Duser.language=en -Duser.region=US This will ensure consistent resource naming and help prevent such errors.
warnings.c6a: We detected signs in the $LOG_FILENAME$ that Create is not compatible with smth (addons or mods adding compat). If you're playing a modpack and have added or updated mods, try reverting those changes or reinstalling the modpack if you don't remember what you changed. Create updated to 6.0 on February 28th, 2025. Addons which previously worked for 5.x almost universally do not work with 6.0 due to significant changes to create. What does that mean for you? Go through all of both addons to create and mods which add create compatibility (such as Supplementaries). Check the release date of the latest version for the mod. If it's after the 28th, you get to keep it/update to it! If there isn't a version released after the 28th, you'll have to choose between dropping that mod or downgrading everything to versions released before the 28th and dropping Create back down as well For best results, check the changelog for the mod The kind folks at create/modrinth have compiled a (mostly) accurate list of addons that have updated to support create 6. Read it $LINK.C6A$!

warnings.codex_erroring_entity: If this happened with an unmodified modpack, consider reporting it to the modpack authors, as this shouldn't happen. To remove the erroring block or entity, you can try temporarily installing the Neruina mod. This will not fix the cause of the issue, but it will let you join the world and remove the problematic entity or block. For Forge and NeoForge, there is an alternative option: Forge: go to "world"/serverconfig/forge-server.toml ("world" being the name of your world) NeoForge: go to config/neoforge-server.toml Enable the appropriate option depending on what is erroring: Set removeErroringBlockEntities = true to remove any BlockEntity that throws an error in its update method. Set removeErroringEntities = true to remove any Entity that throws an error in its tick method.
